question: Two committed identities normalise to one street identity -- 3764|state|48108. Are they two hotels at one doorway, or one building whose Motel 6 identity is stale? NOTHING IS INFERRED HERE. The same-doorway guard added by this order keeps them SEPARATE by default, because each names a different official page, so no merge can happen while this sits unruled.
why_it_was_never_flagged_before: The committed census collision audit compares raw street_identity STRINGS -- '3764 s state st|48108' against '3764 south state street|48108' -- and they differ. address_key, which the exclusion authority and the publication guard both use, normalises them to the same key. The pair has been invisible to the audit since it was created.

sides.identity_key: residence inn by marriott ann arbor south
sides.canonical_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Ann Arbor South

findings.what_it_is: The brand's OWN city locator page -- the exact URL the committed Motel 6 row carries as its official_url.
findings.observed: The page heading reads '6 motels in Ann Arbor MI', and every one of the six listings is in a DIFFERENT city: Farmington Hills, Southgate, Warren, Toledo, ROSSFORD, Southgate. Not one listing is in Ann Arbor, and none is at 3764 S State St.
findings.what_it_supports: Motel 6's own live inventory shows NO property in Ann Arbor. That is the same mechanism that retired Hawthorn Suites Southfield in Pass 2: the brand's own search returns zero branded properties at or near the committed address.
findings.what_it_does_NOT_establish: It does not by itself prove the Residence Inn occupies that building, and it does not date the change. A locator can also drop a property for reasons other than closure.

findings.what_it_is: The Residence Inn's own property page, property code dtwrp.
findings.observed: NOT READ. The page is behind an Akamai bot wall and served no content to the attended browser -- the established Marriott hard lane. Recorded as an access outcome, never as evidence about the property: a wall proves nothing about what is behind it.

attended_evidence_gathered_at_zero_cost.the_weaker_record_of_the_two: The Motel 6 row's official_url is a CITY-level brand page with no property code, bound PAGE_RENDERED. The Residence Inn row carries a real property page with code dtwrp, a phone, and name+address+phone corroboration. If one of the two identities is stale, the evidence points at the Motel 6 row.

recommended_founder_ruling.confidence: MODERATE -- one first-party source, corroborated by the weakness of the Motel 6 record itself, and NOT by a reading of the Residence Inn page, which could not be read.
recommended_founder_ruling.reasoning: Motel 6's own locator lists no Ann Arbor property at all. The committed Motel 6 row has no phone, no property code, and a city-level URL. This is not a pet-policy decision and would create no exclusion.
recommended_founder_ruling.note: A RECOMMENDATION. No ruling is applied by this order, which was told not to infer on this pair.

what_would_settle_it_at_zero_cost: An attended read of the Residence Inn dtwrp page from a session that gets past the Akamai wall -- the Detroit market has broken that wall before with an attended browser -- comparing its STATED street address against 3764 S State St.
A recorded operator telephone call to (734) 590-7500, asking what previously operated at that address.
Neither costs anything. Neither has been done, so the pair stays unruled.

guard_status.effect: 3764|state|48108 is a CONTESTED doorway: both identities name a different official page, so neither may absorb the other and both survive any recensus untouched. The open question cannot silently resolve itself.
